about: Service-page operations: what each one is, what the app does with it today, and what evidence exists per brand family. An operation that changes the car is offered only with exact, per-vehicle, reviewed evidence; none of that exists for any vehicle yet.

generatedFrom.classifiers: MileageSignalClassifier + ServiceMetricClassifier, as compiled in this test run
generatedFrom.note: OBDb-derived tables: CC BY-SA 4.0, attribution and share-alike apply (see README.md).

principle: Reading is separated from writing. A read needs a public definition for the exact model; a write that changes the car needs exact, per-vehicle, reviewed evidence (exact module and address, exact request bytes, exact positive reply, read-back after the reset, safety preconditions, hashed evidence) and none exists for any vehicle. Until then the app shows the owner's own documented steps and says plainly that it sent nothing. A percentage other than 100 is never offered on the strength of a reset alone: setting a chosen value is a different capability that a module has to be documented to accept.

operationTypes.label: Read oil life remaining (%)
operationTypes.meaning: A percentage that shrinks as the oil ages; 100 = fresh oil.

operationTypes.label: Read oil degradation (%)
operationTypes.meaning: A percentage that grows as the oil wears; 0 = fresh oil. The opposite scale of the previous one.

operationTypes.label: Read service distance, days, distance since the oil change, interval, maintenance counters
operationTypes.meaning: Counters and remaining distances the module reports. Some count down, some count up; the name states which.

operationTypes.label: Reset the oil-life monitor to 100%
operationTypes.meaning: Tells the oil-life monitor that the oil was changed. After it the remaining life is 100% (or the degradation 0%).

operationTypes.label: Set the oil life to a chosen percentage (for example 50%)
operationTypes.meaning: Writes a value other than 'new oil'. Possible only where the module is documented to accept it. A reset that works says nothing about this.

operationTypes.label: Reset the service-interval counters (distance and time)
operationTypes.meaning: Restarts the distance and time counters behind a 'Service due' display (VAG service interval indicator, ASSYST, BMW CBS items, Honda Maintenance Minder items).

operationTypes.label: Reset the inspection reminder
operationTypes.meaning: On some brands the inspection distance and time are separate from the oil service (VAG).

operationTypes.label: Dismiss a 'Service due' / 'Maintenance required' message
operationTypes.meaning: Whether dismissing the message also restarts the counters is vehicle-specific and has to come from that vehicle's own documentation; the app never assumes it.

operationTypes.label: Change the configured service interval
operationTypes.meaning: A configuration change (for example a maximum distance in km). Not offered.

currentAppBehaviour.how: Service page. The normal refresh sends the non-debug OBDb definitions of the exact model, plus the brand-wide identifiers of the make (labelled research-level evidence). With a verified model year it uses the flag and the filter of THAT year (OBDb's dbgfilter and filter, from Resources/Raw/obdb_year_evidence.json): a request that does not apply to the year is not sent, a request OBDb still flags debug in that year is research-level, and a reply recorded in OBDb's tests for the year is named in the reading's detail. A definition whose recorded replies show it holds something else than its name says is never shown (the BMW 'Distance since last oil change' is the odometer). A value is shown only after an identifier-matching positive reply with a plausible figure (0 to 100).
Own kind and own row 'Engine oil degradation (higher = more worn)' with an explaining line. It is not a reset target: the write path refuses anything that is not remaining life.
Same path as above, one row per kind with the unit the module reports.

165 shipped procedures (manual, from owner's manuals and manufacturer documents). Two automatic write paths exist in code and both are closed by design: the GMLAN write needs a reviewed entry (ReviewedGmOilLifeResets is empty, so no vehicle passes CanResetLearnedOilLife), and the catalog write-back needs a whitelisted identifier (OBDService.WritableServiceDids is an empty set, and ServiceSafetyTests asserts that it stays empty).
The 50% button is visible only when a reviewed entry states AllowsPercentTargets; the sender refuses any target other than 100 otherwise. No entry exists. Implemented in this work.
Guides for Maintenance Minder, ASSYST / ASSYST PLUS, BMW service indicator, VAG service reminder and others. Nothing is sent to the car.
One inspection-reminder guide for the VW group; the catalog marks it as a separate operation from the oil service.
As documented per vehicle in the guide text; the app does not claim an effect the documentation does not state.
No code path, no catalog entry.

diagnosticWriteOperations.productionRule: Only exact, source-backed, vehicle/ECU-specific operations may be placed in 'operations'. Research candidates are intentionally non-executable and are ignored by the current app loader.
promotionChecklist: Exact ECU definition and address verified
Exact request bytes captured or documented
Manufacturer catalog upgraded to VerifiedService for that definition

familyResearchCandidates.targetFunction: Oil service and inspection interval reset
Oil and scheduled maintenance reminder reset

brandFamilies.label: GM (Chevrolet, GMC, Buick, Cadillac, Holden, Opel / Vauxhall)

read.detail: OBDb defines 'Oil life remaining' (service 22, percent). Replies are recorded for 22 4DC0 at module 0x11 (29-bit, header DA11) on Cadillac Escalade 2022, Corvette 2024-2025, Silverado 1500 2022-2026, Silverado 2500 2025, Tahoe, GMC Canyon, Sierra 2500HD, Terrain 2026 and Yukon. The older 7E0 requests (4DC0, and 119F for the Volt) are still flagged debug and nothing is recorded for them; OBDb decodes 119F as a raw percentage while the app decodes it as A*100/255, which needs a car to settle.

guidedReset.detail: Engine Oil Life System procedures for Equinox, Silverado, Enclave, XT5, Volt and Opel Mokka X are shipped. GM's bulletin PIP5282A / 18-NA-125 describes what the monitor counts (revolutions, mileage since the reset capped at 7,500 miles from model year 2013 except the Volt, time: one year, two for the Volt).

diagnosticReset.status: tool function documented, request not published
diagnosticReset.detail: GM bulletin 12312A (August 2013, read in full) has dealers reprogram the engine control module and then use a scan tool to reset the Engine Oil Life Remaining back to the percentage recorded before: the tool function exists and the engine control module is the executing module. The request is not published. Community GMLAN research (no licence) lists a gateway message 0x1F1 'Engine oil life reset request' that also carries the remote-start request and the immobilizer pre-release password: the app never sends it. A forum post with a Mode 22 request is unverified and was not used. A consumer app (Car Scanner) lists a 'Reset service reminder' function for GM cars with CAN bus; its page shows no protocol detail.

setPercent.status: documented for GM's own tool on four vehicle groups
setPercent.detail: The same bulletin restores a recorded percentage, so GM's tool sets a chosen value on 2010-2011 Buick LaCrosse, 2011-2012 Buick Regal, 2010-2012 Chevrolet Equinox and GMC Terrain with the 2.4L engines (RPO LAF, LEA, LUK). No request is published and nothing says that other engines accept a chosen value. The app offers no percentage other than the reset.

read.detail: 'Oil life remaining' (22 054B, percent): replies are recorded for 33 Ford and Lincoln vehicles (for example F-150 2014-2026, Escape and Kuga 2014-2025, Expedition 2018-2025, Mustang 2016, 2019, 2024-2026, Transit, Bronco, Maverick). For several vehicles OBDb flags the definition debug in the years in between. Also 'Distance since last oil change' (22 0542; recorded for 9 Fords) and, for Mazda, 22 0519 (recorded for the Mazda 3, 6 and CX-5).

guidedReset.detail: Intelligent Oil Life Monitor (Bronco, Bronco Sport, Maverick) and oil-change-indicator reset (Focus 2018) guides are shipped.

diagnosticReset.detail: FORScan's change history lists per-vehicle PCM service procedures 'Reset oil change indicator' (Ranger and Everest diesel, EcoSport EU 1.5 TDCi, Edge 2.0 TDCi, Ka 1.5 TDCi, Fiesta Mk7 TDCi, Galaxy / S-Max, Territory and others) and 'Reset Engine Oil Deterioration Learned Value' (Mazda 3 / 5 / 6 / CX-3 / CX-5 / CX-7 diesels and F-Series 6.7 Powerstroke); the request is not public. On the dashboard path opendbc (MIT) shows the mechanism: the cluster message 0x430 carries the reset-request bit EngOilLife_B_RqReset (which also sits next to the odometer, so imitating it would write a whole cluster frame: never done) and the PCM answers with the oil-service message states ResetInProgress and ResetComplete (diesel) or the percentage (petrol). Ford's bulletins treat the reminder reset as an owner's-manual step. On a Mazda diesel the learned value is the oil dilution (fuel in oil), not a percentage of oil life; the owner method for the SKYACTIV-D 2.2 is in the official manual.

setPercent.detail: No source describes setting a chosen oil-life value on these vehicles.

brandFamilies.label: Stellantis / FCA / PSA (Jeep, Dodge, Ram, Chrysler, Fiat, Alfa Romeo, Peugeot, Citroen)

read.detail: 'Engine oil degradation' (22 3813 at module DA10, percent) grows with wear; replies are recorded for the Fiat 500X (2019, 2021) and the Jeep Renegade (2018-2019). PSA vehicles add 'Distance to next oil change' and a severe-conditions mileage counter, all still debug.

guidedReset.detail: RAM 2500 / 3500, Chrysler 300 and Pacifica, Dodge Challenger / Charger / Durango oil-life reset guides, and Peugeot / Citroen service-indicator zeroing guides are shipped.

diagnosticReset.status: tool routines named, request not published
diagnosticReset.detail: Stellantis STAR case S2309000009 (October 2023, read in full) has the technician run two routines of the dealer tool, both under 'Miscellaneous Functions': 'Reset Service Information' in the instrument panel cluster and 'Reset oil change indicator' in the PCM. No identifier is published. arduino-psa-diag (GPL-3.0, cloned and searched) documents session and unlock services for PSA coding zones and has no service reset; its data is quarantined and was not used.

brandFamilies.label: VAG (Volkswagen, Audi, Seat, Cupra, Skoda, Porsche, Bentley)

read.detail: OBDb defines many oil-level signals (millimetres, percent) for the group, and none for remaining oil life or a service interval. The service interval indicator lives in the instrument cluster and is reached through cluster adaptation channels (Ross-Tech), not through a public read definition.

guidedReset.detail: VW Jetta 2021 service-reminder bulletin, CUPRA Formentor, Skoda guides and a separate inspection-reminder guide are shipped. US bulletins warn that a manual oil-service reset on a flexible-service car switches the display to a fixed interval, that the interval between services must not be reset, and that disconnecting the battery interrupts the next-service calculation.

diagnosticReset.detail: Ross-Tech documents, in the instrument cluster (module 17, adaptation), the items by name: 'ESI: Resetting ESI' (oil service), 'FIX: Distance covered since last mileage-dependent inspection' and 'FIX: Time since last time-dependent inspection' (set to 0), and 'SID / SIA: maximum value of distance / time to service' (the interval in km); older cars use numbered channels (02, or 05 to 08). No identifier or byte appears, and the vis4vag.com operation pages ('Reset of service interval QI', 'Reset of variable oil change interval QI6') are paywalled with the values masked.

setPercent.detail: The same channels also hold the maximum distance and time to service (an interval setting, in km). It is a separate operation (set.service-interval) and is not offered.

read.detail: 'Distance since last oil change' (22 DFE7, module 0x19) is listed for 19 BMW and 4 MINI models and the Toyota GR Supra, but recorded replies (343, BMW 3, 5, 7 Series, X3, X5) have the size of an odometer, not of a service interval: the app no longer shows it as an oil-change distance.

guidedReset.detail: A BMW service-indicator / CBS guide is shipped.

diagnosticReset.detail: BMW's own bulletins (SI B62 06 13, read in full) show that on F01-F30 cars the CBS due dates for Oil Service and Check Vehicle are held in the instrument cluster, that the cluster's test function #25 'Software reset' repairs a software fault (a due date that falls back to 01/2000) and is not a service reset, and that ISTA has a test plan for resetting and adjusting the CBS data. The EDIABAS description of a diesel DME lists CBS_RESET (UDS 2E; item, availability percentage, number of services, target month and year, remaining distance with unit, forecast intervals), CBS_RESET_DATEN_LESEN (22 4050), STEUERN_CBS_DATEN_SICHERN (31 01 F0ED), STATUS_CBS_DATEN_SICHERN (31 03 F0ED), STATUS_CBSMOTOROELHIST (22 404F) and STATUS_CODIERUNG_OEL (22 3701). The identifier CBS_RESET writes is not shown, and the page, derived from BMW's proprietary description file, has no licence.

read.detail: 'Distance to next service' (22 6504 at 7E5) has recorded replies for the EQB and EQV (8,000 to 40,000 km); other Mercedes and smart definitions are debug.

guidedReset.detail: ASSYST / ASSYST PLUS guides, including the Sprinter (906) from an official Mercedes-Benz Vans document.

diagnosticReset.detail: The official Sprinter maintenance booklets (mbvans.com, 2010-2014) say the authorized dealer resets the ASSYST service interval display, and warn of engine damage if it is reset without the service. No official or open routine is published; workshop blogs describe XENTRY menus and cluster key sequences and disagree.

read.detail: 'Distance since oil change' (21 41 at 7C0): replies are recorded for 16 Toyota and Lexus models (0 to 28,968 km). 'Estimated distance to oil change' is still debug.

guidedReset.detail: Maintenance-required light procedures for Toyota, Lexus and Scion are shipped.

diagnosticReset.evidence: E3 (the reminder is cleared from the display), E0 (request)
diagnosticReset.detail: A 2023 Lexus bulletin clears the Maintenance Required reminder from the multi-information display's vehicle settings menu; Techstream appears in the bulletins for other jobs, not for this one.

read.detail: 'Maintenance, <item>' for nine items (oil and filter, air cleaner, cabin filter, coolant, brake fluid, transmission fluid, spark plugs and valves, tire rotation, general inspection) at 22 7060, module DA60: replies are recorded for the Accord, Civic and Clarity (values 0 to 9,999). The definition gives no unit, so the page shows the number as the module reports it.

guidedReset.detail: Maintenance Minder procedures (Acura RDX 2023, TLX 2021 and others) are shipped.

diagnosticReset.detail: Honda bulletins name the older HDS path 'Body Electrical, Adjustment, Maintenance Minder, Reset, then the maintenance sub-item', and for newer cars either i-HDS or the multi-information display depending on the item (bulletin 23-073). No request is published.

read.detail: 'Estimated distance to oil change' (km) for several models, nearly all flagged debug.

guidedReset.detail: Centre information display maintenance-screen guides (Legacy / Outback 2020) are shipped.

read.detail: Oil change interval, range and history in km, miles or months, 'Maintenance autonomy' values and 'Maintenance mode'. Several definitions give a kilometre name with a mile unit or a month value with the unit 'scalar'.

guidedReset.detail: Dacia and Renault-family guides are shipped where an exact source exists.

brandFamilies.label: Hyundai, Kia, Genesis, Nissan, Infiniti, Mitsubishi, Suzuki

read.detail: The catalog has no oil-life, service-distance or maintenance signal for these makes.

guidedReset.detail: Cluster-menu and button procedures are shipped for Kia (ten), Hyundai, Genesis, Nissan, Infiniti, Mitsubishi and Suzuki.

diagnosticReset.detail: Kia TSB ELE209 (Rev 3, 2022): for 2019MY and later the dealer tool KDS, 'Cluster Module', 'S/W Management', 'Service Reminder Setting' changes the service type from workshop to customer and takes the mileage and time. TSB ENG241 (2022): on 2023MY and later cars with the oil life management system the owner resets from the head unit ('Vehicle Settings', 'Cluster', 'Oil Change Reminder', 'Reset'). Nothing is published about the wire.

gaps.note: A guide tells the owner what to press; a read definition tells the app where a value is. The two are independent, so a brand can have either, both or neither.

negativeFindings.finding: No open or documented raw request (UDS 0x2E / 0x31, KWP2000, GMLAN) for resetting an oil-life monitor or a service reminder was found for any brand.
searched: GM bulletins and Mode 22 oil-life discussions
generic UDS oil-service reset on GitHub
FORScan, Ross-Tech, Toyota and Honda resets
negativeFindings.result: Procedure-level descriptions and proof that closed tools can do it, nothing that could be used without guessing bytes.

negativeFindings.finding: SAE J1979 has no PID for oil life, a service interval or a maintenance reminder. The only oil-related standard PID is 5C, engine oil temperature.
searched: Wikipedia OBD-II PIDs, Mode 01 table and the other modes
negativeFindings.result: Confirmed from the page; the standard itself (paid) was not read.

negativeFindings.finding: All OBDb commands are read services. Of 226,798 signals in the default signal sets (880 vehicle repositories read, 5 unreadable; 609 of them define at least one signal), 186,617 use service 22, 39,074 use service 21 and 1,107 use service 01. There is no write, routine or security-access command.
searched: OBDb signalsets/v3/default.json of every vehicle repository
negativeFindings.result: Counted with research/tools/tally-obdb-services.js; year-range override files were not downloaded. The shipped catalog holds 556 vehicles, fewer than upstream defines today.

negativeFindings.finding: The shipped catalog cannot restrict a row to a model year: OBDb's 'filter' and 'dbgfilter' are absent from all 157,229 rows.
searched: raw_json of every OBDb row in the shipped catalog
negativeFindings.result: A row applies to the model whatever the year. See next-steps.md.

negativeFindings.finding: No source published by a vehicle maker, an open-source project or a tool vendor gives the request of an oil-life or service-reminder reset in a form that may be used.
searched: NHTSA-hosted bulletins of GM, BMW, Kia, Stellantis, Ford, Toyota/Lexus, Honda and VAG (read in full)
GitHub repository search for oil, service and CBS resets (ten queries)
arduino-psa-diag (cloned and searched), l77rodeo/gmlan (README), opendbc (grep of every DBC)
FORScan forum threads (two read, two blocked)
Ross-Tech wiki pages, the EDIABAS description of a DME, the Mazda owner's manual
negativeFindings.result: Function names, executing modules and verification paths. The one place with job structure (BMW CBS_RESET) does not show the written identifier and has no licence.

negativeFindings.finding: The wire-level mechanism of the dashboard reset is a broadcast on Ford (cluster message 0x430, bit EngOilLife_B_RqReset) and GM (gateway message 0x1F1). Neither can be imitated safely: the Ford frame also carries the odometer, the GM frame also carries a remote-start request and the immobilizer pre-release password.
negativeFindings.result: Recorded as the mechanism and as a way to recognise a reset in a recording; never sent.
